minutes.headline: Finance Committee leans to defer streetlights and most capital, keep culvert and cruiser, and put free cash in reserve fund.
minutes.summary: Ahead of the town meeting, the committee discussed hedging against a possible state aid cut and where to put unappropriated free cash. Members broadly favored the reserve fund over stabilization, not recommending the streetlight article, and deferring most of the capital plan except the culvert and a police cruiser. They also reviewed a charge for a debt subcommittee.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee leaned toward deferring most of the capital plan, keeping only the culvert and a marked police cruiser, and putting the difference in the reserve fund.
The committee voted to recommend not approving article 21, the streetlight article; the vote count was not audible in the captions.
The committee voted to make no recommendation on the budget adjustment article and on article 9, the sewer enterprise article.
Members discussed a hedge against a possible state aid cut; the budget was built for a smaller cut than the larger one also discussed.
A debt subcommittee is to be formed with two members, Peter and Dave.

why_it_matters: Deferring capital projects and holding free cash in the reserve fund keeps the town's options open if state aid falls, but pushes the deferred projects into later years' budgets.
The streetlight article and the capital choices are items Town Meeting voters will be asked to decide, and the committee's recommendations shape what appears on that warrant.
watch_next: Town Meeting votes on article 21, streetlights, and on the capital plan items the committee leans to defer.
The charge and first work of the new debt subcommittee.
